summary: Dependency-confusion recon beacon exfiltrates host metadata on install
details: @ecg-internal/js-react-i18n@2.0.0 is a dependency-confusion probe targeting an internal-looking npm scope. The package has no real functionality: its main entry (index.js) exports a Proxy that returns a no-op for every property access, allowing consumer builds to silently succeed. On install, the postinstall lifecycle script runs beacon.cjs, which POSTs a JSON payload containing os.hostname(), __dirname (install path), process.cwd(), the package name, and the Node version to a hardcoded plain-HTTP bare-IP collector at http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The same fire() function is also invoked from index.js, so the beacon fires both on `npm install` (via postinstall) and when the module is required. The combination of a scoped-internal name, an inert Proxy stub, and an install-time beacon to a bare-IP endpoint is the canonical dependency-confusion reconnaissance shape, enumerating internal build environments that resolve the public package instead of a private one.
